_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc, and a short quote from the saved document. derived = arithmetic done here from sourced values; is_derived marks a value that is itself DERIVED. alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). Every quote was machine-checked against the saved file's extracted text (whitespace/glyph-normalised).
_meta.quote_normalisation: PDF text from pdftotext (layout, raw and default modes; line-break hyphenation joined or kept); ADS scans without a text layer (AS94, FS95, AR92) OCRed with tesseract 5.5.1 at 300 dpi -- quotes are the OCR text, numbers checked on the page images; HTML text by tag stripping (script bodies kept; table cells joined with " | "); plain-text files (maskgen opticdef.dat, IRAF identify databases) verbatim; FITS tables via an astropy text dump of header cards and rows ("row r: a00=... a01=..."). NFKC; dashes, quotes, primes (two primes / double prime -> "), degree glyphs, ~, x, u normalised; whitespace removed. ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces.

grism_model_verdict.LDSS-3: VPH grisms = model (b) exactly (maskgen EGRISM: faces at -A/+A, grating at 0 deg, identical prisms); verified against measured arc solutions (centre wavelength <= 27 A, dispersion <= 0.6 %, +/-2 arcmin slits <= 25 A). Old LDSS-2 BK7 grisms = model (a) exactly.
grism_model_verdict.FORS2: Standard grisms = surface-relief, but NOT plain model (a): entrance face tilted 7.5 deg (FS95); ESO data require the tilt in the dispersion plane with the grating-face normal at (phi - 7.5 deg) to the axis: m G lambda0 = n sin(phi - eps') - sin(phi - eps), sin eps' = sin(eps)/n. Plain (a) gives lambda0 0.4-0.8 % low and dispersion 4-11 % high. VPH grisms = model (b) in kind; geometry NOT FOUND.

ldss3.title: Magellan II (Clay) / LDSS-3 (imaging multi-slit spectrograph; straight-through focal reducer with three VPH grisms between prism pairs)
ldss3.recommended_preset: VPH-All grism (the general-purpose low-resolution mode), 0.75" slit (LCO resolution table) -- 1.0" is the usual MOS width, ~17 slits per mask (DERIVED mean of 35 published masks; 20-25 in another survey), Magellan Clay 6.5 m at f/11 (maskgen focal length 71475.8 mm -> 2.886 "/mm), refractive collimator 746.8 mm (maskgen; 745.935 nominal), DERIVED beam 67.9 mm, camera 173.08 mm (final f/2.5), LDSS-3C Fermilab CCD 2048 x 4096 x 15 um with the 4096-px axis along the dispersion, 1x1 binning. Grism = model (b) exactly: VPH layer normal to the axis between two fused-silica prisms of apex 16.30 deg (outer faces at -16.30/+16.30 deg), 400 l/mm, m = 1 -> DERIVED lambda0 = 6584 A. Validate against: LCO table R = 860 (0.75"), 1.890 A/px, 4250-10000 A, "central" 7100 A; and the measured 2007 arc solution through the centre slit: lambda at detector centre 6588 A, local 2.040 A/px (DERIVED from 36 identified lines), 0.189 "/px. The maskgen geometry reproduces all three grisms' measured arcs (centre wavelength to <= 27 A, dispersion to <= 0.6 %, +/-2 arcmin slits to <= 25 A; Notes). Alternatives: VPH-Blue (1090 l/mm, 2 x 24.00 deg S-LAL7 prisms; lambda0 5166 A; 0.682 A/px, R 1900, 3800-6200 A) and VPH-Red (665 l/mm in maskgen / 660 nominal, 2 x 24.00 deg S-LAL7; lambda0 8294 A; 1.175 A/px, R 1810, 6000-10000 A, with OG590).

Validation of the geometry against measured data (DERIVED here): fitting x = x0 + f_cam tan(phi(lambda)) to the identified arc lines of the three centre-slit databases with the maskgen grism parameters and only (x0, f_cam) free gives f_cam = 172.36 mm (VPH-All, rms 1.4 px over 36 lines), 172.40 mm (VPH-Blue, rms 2.0 px), 171.97 mm (VPH-Red at 665 l/mm, rms 1.0 px; 172.97 mm and rms 1.4 px at 660 l/mm) -- within 0.6 % of maskgen's 173.076 mm. The predicted wavelength at the detector centre for slits 2 arcmin off-centre matches the measured off-axis databases to <= 25 A (performance table).

Glass: maskgen stores n^2 as a Laurent series in lambda^-2 (form in the glass section); its S-LAL7 matches the OHARA S-LAL7 Sellmeier to <= 7e-6 in 0.49-0.85 um and 1.7e-4 at 0.365 um, and its Fused_Silica matches Malitson (1965) to <= 6e-6. S-LAL7 is not in the round-1 glass list: OHARA Sellmeier coefficients are given below (SCHOTT N-LAK7 has the same nd 1.65160 but is a different melt).

Detector history: the pre-2014 LDSS-3 CCD had at least 4064 px along the dispersion (the 2007 arc databases span x = 1..4064; its type is not documented in the saved sources); LDSS-3C (2014-) uses the Fermilab 2k x 4k S3-171 with the 4096-px axis along the dispersion and the 6.4 arcmin spatial trim. Both have 15 um pixels, so the 2007 dispersion solutions apply per pixel.

The VPH grism wavelength coverage "varies substantially over the detector" (LUM): slits offset along the dispersion by +/-2 arcmin shift the spectrum by about +/-1300 A for VPH-All (measured; reproduced by the model through the field angle).

Grism = surface-relief, 300 gr/mm, m = 1, prism angle 21 deg, glass FK5 (design table; use N-FK5/FK5HTi), groove angle 17.5 deg -- BUT the real FORS grisms are NOT pure model (a): "the entrance surfaces are all tilted by 7.5 deg" (FS95), and ESO's own numbers (manual table and pipeline calibration) are reproduced only if that tilt lies in the dispersion plane with the grating face at (prism angle - 7.5 deg) to the optical axis: m G lambda0 = n sin(phi - eps') - sin(phi - eps), sin eps' = sin(7.5 deg)/n. Design vs operational parameters: FS95 300V 110 A/mm, R 420 (no filter) and 112, R 500 (GG435); FUM117 112 A/mm, R 440. FS95 600B R 815 vs FUM117 780. FS95 300I range 600-1140 nm vs FUM117 6000-11000 A.
Dispersion units: FUM117 A/pixel is per unbinned 15-um pixel (DERIVED: 112 A/mm x 0.015 mm = 1.68), N13 quotes the 2x2-binned value 3.36 A/pixel for 300V.
VPH dispersions: manual nominal values vs pipeline-measured (1200R 0.38 vs 0.365; 600RI 0.83 vs 0.815; 600z 0.81 vs 0.802 A/px) -- 2-4 % differences.
notes: Grism model fit: the FORS standard grisms are surface-relief (ruled replica) grisms -- model (a) in kind -- but with the entrance face tilted 7.5 deg (FS95). Tested against ESO's numbers (DERIVED, table below), the tilt must lie in the dispersion plane and rotate the whole grism so that the grating-face normal is at (phi - 7.5 deg) from the optical axis. Exact geometry for the explorer: beam along the axis meets the entrance face at 7.5 deg incidence, refracts to eps' = asin(sin 7.5 deg / n) inside, meets the ruled hypotenuse at internal incidence (phi - eps'), diffracts into air at angle beta from the grating normal; undeviated when beta = phi - 7.5 deg, i.e. m G lambda0 = n sin(phi - eps') - sin(phi - 7.5 deg). Equivalently: model (a) with an extra entrance-face tilt parameter eps = 7.5 deg applied with the opposite sense to the apex.

Measured vs model (DERIVED; measured = pipeline master distortion table at the CCD centre, chip 1): 600B 4629 A / 0.7476 A/px vs tilted 4629 / 0.7490 vs plain-(a) 4604 / 0.6933; 300V 5849 / 1.6549 vs 5858 / 1.6639 vs 5826 / 1.5968; 300I 8574 / 1.6101 vs 8584 / 1.6249 vs 8538 / 1.5366; 150I 7176 / 3.4118 vs 7156 / 3.4370 vs 7117 / 3.3750; 600I 7936 / 0.6594 vs 7940 / 0.6648 vs 7901 / 0.5898. Opposite tilt sense (grating face turned away): same lambda0, dispersion 5-23 % too low. Glasses: N-FK5 for FK5, LF5, N-BAK2 for BaK2, SF5, N-K5 for K5, F2HT for F2 (SCOL).

The FS95 Table 1 numbers were read from the page image (OCR garbles 17.5, 26.7, 11.5 and the column header "phi prism angle, psi groove angle"). FS95 numbers its grisms std. 1-7 and cross-disperser I-III and does not use ESO names: the identification std. 1 = 600B, cross II (F2) = 600V, std. 2 = 600R, std. 3 = 600I, std. 5 = 300V, std. 6 = 300I, std. 7 = 150I is DERIVED by matching lines/mm, wavelength range and A/mm with FUM117 Table 2.4 (600B also by A98: "600 lines/mm blazed in the blue"), and is confirmed by the tilted model reproducing ESO's centre wavelengths to <= 20 A. Cross-dispersers I-III served the FORS2 echelle mode, later decommissioned.

Pipeline distortion tables: FPM Sec. 7.6 defines them (x = sum_r c_r (lambda - lambda_o)^r, c_r a bivariate quadratic in CCD position for r = 1..5, in focal-plane position for r = 0). The calibration frames are 2x2 binned (BINX = 2), so c1 is in binned pixels per A; it was evaluated at the reference-wavelength position (x0 = c0, y0 = 119 binned px, the field centre on chip 1 per FUM117 "y-pixel ~238 ... unbinned"). Using the a00 term alone (CCD corner) would give 0.69 A/px for 600B -- that reading is wrong.
The explorer's slit-image R should include the grism anamorphic factor of the tilted geometry (beam out/in = 0.952-0.991 at lambda0; DERIVED). ESO's R column omits it (R = lambda/(slit px x A/px)).
